name: ReViT
backbones: DeiT-S; LV-ViT-S; MotionFormer ViT-B; MotionFormer ViT-L
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 -0.1 at 50% acceleration (Intro; numbers only in Fig. 5 and Fig. 8)
notes: A Token-Length Assigner (small EfficientNet-B0) predicts per image which of 14x14, 10x10 or 7x7 token grids to use; the Resizable-ViT handles all lengths with token-length-aware LayerNorm and self-distillation. DeiT-S ImageNet results appear only as accuracy-throughput plots (RTX 3090, batch 32), no table, so top-1, GFLOPs and throughput cannot be copied. No code URL. ECML PKDD 2023 per arXiv comment.
evidence: "we introduce a method for adaptively assigning token length for each image at test time to accelerate inference speed" (Abstract); "we train a lightweight Token-Length Assigner (TLA) that allocates the optimal token length for each image during inference" (Abstract); "The throughput is measured on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPU with batch size fixed to 32" (Fig. 5); "Our proposed ReViT is almost a cheap as training the baseline DeiT-S" (Fig. 7)

name: CF-ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 1.8 GFLOPs (eta=0.5; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Coarse stage with 7x7 patches; if the confidence is below eta, the top-50% informative coarse patches (global class attention, EMA over encoders) are re-split 2x2 and a fine stage runs with feature reuse. Throughput on one A100 with batch 1024. Training follows the DeiT recipe (all patches fine-split for the first 200 epochs, then informative re-splitting); the paper does not use a pre-trained checkpoint, so training is taken as from scratch.
evidence: "At coarse inference stage, an input image is split into a small-length patch sequence for a computationally economical classification. If not well recognized, the informative patches are identified and further re-split in a fine-grained granularity" (Abstract); "it is natural to use the class attention a0k as a score to indicate if a token is informative" (Coarse Inference Stage); "if pcj >= eta, the inference will terminate" (Coarse Inference Stage); "All training settings of our CF-ViT, such as image processing, learning rate, etc, are to follow these of DeiT and LV-ViT" (Implementation Details)

name: TPS
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-T; LV-ViT-S; PS-ViT; PVT-T; PVT-S; CvT-13; CvT-21
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.1 at 3.0 GFLOPs (dTPS, 100 fine-tuning epochs; baseline 79.8 at 4.6); eTPS 79.7 at 3.0 (30 epochs)
notes: Prune then squeeze: dTPS scores tokens with DynamicViT's learned head, eTPS with class-token attention; each pruned token is matched (cosine) to its nearest reserved host token and fused with similarity weights, keeping a constant shape. Fine-tuned 30 or 100 epochs from pre-trained weights. Throughput (RTX 2080Ti, batch 32) is shown only in figures; the text gives 1745 img/s for DeiT-S at the 35% FLOPs budget, not for the 3.0 GFLOPs row.
evidence: "Firstly, TPS adopts pruning to get the reserved and pruned subsets. Secondly, TPS squeezes the information of pruned tokens into partial reserved tokens via the unidirectional nearest-neighbor matching and similarity-based fusing steps" (Abstract); "dTPS adopts the learnable token score prediction head from dynamicViT ... eTPS utilizes the class token attention values to measure tokens' importance" (3.2); "we devise the token selection policy using the Top-k operation with a fixed given token reduction ratio" (3.2); "The model is initialized with pre-trained models' weights and fine-tuned with different token pruning locations and keeping ratios" (4)

name: BAT
notes: Token decoupling and merging at layers 4/7/10: class attention splits attentive and inattentive tokens; inattentive tokens are clustered by a simplified density-peak clustering and combined by attention-weighted sum; the top-K most similar attentive pairs are fused. No token is simply dropped. Trained from scratch for 300 epochs on 8 V100 with a cosine keep-rate schedule. Throughput on one V100 with batch 256. No code URL in the paper.
evidence: "According to the class token attention, we decouple the attentive and inattentive tokens. In addition to preserve the most discriminative local tokens, we merge similar inattentive tokens and match homogeneous attentive tokens to maximize the token diversity" (Abstract); "we select top-K most similar token pairs as homogeneous tokens. Finally, we combine each pair of tokens into a new token" (4.4); "all of our models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs on 8 NVIDIA V100" (5.1)

name: STViT
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; Swin-T; Swin-S; Swin-B; LV-ViT-S; Video Swin-T; Video Swin-S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.8 at 1.91 GFLOPs (16 semantic tokens; baseline 79.8 at 4.58)
notes: No per-token scoring: a semantic token generation module (two transformer layers at blocks 5-6 of DeiT) turns the 196 image tokens into 16 semantic tokens, initialised by intra/inter-window spatial pooling and refined by attention with the image tokens as keys and values; the image tokens are then discarded. STViT-R adds a recovery module and dumbbell units that restore the full-resolution map for COCO detection and segmentation (Swin). Throughput on a V100 with batch 128. Trained from scratch for 300 epochs.
evidence: "The semantic tokens represent cluster centers, and they are initialized by pooling image tokens in space and recovered by attention" (Abstract); "After the STGM, the image tokens X can be discarded, and only semantic tokens S with high-level semantic information are used in all the subsequent transformers" (3.1); "we design a STViT-R(ecover) network to restore the detailed spatial information based on the STViT, making it work for downstream tasks" (Abstract); "All the models are trained from scratch for 300 epochs" (4.1)

name: SparseViT
main_result: Swin-T (BEVDet, nuScenes): mAP 31.2 at 23.8 ms (baseline 31.2 at 36.4 ms, RTX A6000)
notes: Window-level activation pruning for Swin: windows are ranked by the L2 norm of their activations (score computed once per stage), only the top windows run MHSA, FFN and LN, and unselected windows keep duplicated features so the dense feature map survives (the paper calls this pruning; in the table vocabulary the windows halt). Per-layer sparsity (0-80%) is found by evolutionary search under a #MACs or measured-latency constraint after sparsity-aware adaptation, then the model is fine-tuned. Tasks: nuScenes 3D detection, COCO instance segmentation, Cityscapes semantic segmentation. Backbone latency on one RTX A6000; batch size not stated. No DeiT-S results; the code cell is the project page given in the paper.
evidence: "we define the importance of each window as its L2 activation magnitude" (3.2); "To mitigate information loss due to coarse-grained window pruning, we simply duplicate the features of the unselected windows" (3.2); "we make use of the evolutionary search to explore the best per-layer pruning ratios under a resource constraint" (1); "we finetune the model with the fixed sparsity configurations identified in the search process until convergence" (3.3)

name: SuperViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 80.0 at 2.3 GFLOPs (14x14 tokens, keep rate 0.5; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: One model is trained for four token grids (8x8 to 14x14, patches resized by bilinear interpolation into a shared embedding) times three keep rates {1.0, 0.7, 0.5}; tokens are dropped by class attention at blocks 4/7/10. At inference one (grid, keep rate) pair is picked for the available hardware budget, so each run is a fixed schedule. Throughput on one A100 with batch 512. Trained from scratch following the DeiT/LV-ViT recipes (4.1 days on 4 A100 for DeiT-S).
evidence: "the trained ViT model, termed super vision transformer (SuperViT), is empowered with the versatile ability to solve incoming patches of multiple sizes as well as preserve informative tokens with multiple keeping rates" (Abstract); "we directly preserve tokens with larger attention values in this paper" (3.2.2); "All the training strategies, such as data augmentation, regularization and optimizer, strictly follow the original settings of DeiT" (4.1)

name: HeatViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.34 at 2.64 GMACs (HeatViT-S2, 1.74x; baseline 79.8 at 4.6 GMACs; 8-bit)
notes: Token selector = multi-head token classifier (MLP per head, attention-based head weighting, Gumbel-softmax keep/prune mask with threshold 0.5) plus a token packager that averages non-informative tokens into one package token; the count varies per image. Selectors are inserted from the last block backwards and the pruning rate of each block is raised until the accuracy drop exceeds 0.5% or the latency target is met; a latency-sparsity loss uses a latency table measured on the Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA; similar selectors are merged into 3-4 stages. Costs are GMACs, not GFLOPs. deits_throughput is FPS on the ZCU102 FPGA with 8-bit quantisation (Table VI); Jetson TX2 CPU/GPU speedups also given; batch size not stated. No code URL.
evidence: "we first design an effective attention-based multi-head token selector, which can be progressively inserted before transformer blocks to dynamically identify and consolidate the non-informative tokens from input images" (Abstract); "we apply a token packaging step that summarizes non-informative tokens (predicted by the classifier) into a package token instead of completely discarding them" (IV-B); "we propose a latency-aware multi-stage training strategy to determine the transformer blocks for inserting token selectors and optimize the desired (average) pruning rates for inserted token selectors" (Abstract); "Our training strategy is conducted as fine-tuning on pre-trained ViTs" (I)

name: GTP-ViT
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; ViT-B/8; ViT-Medium-GAP
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.5 at 3.4 GMACs (P=8 tokens per layer, no finetuning; baseline 79.8 at 4.6)
notes: Scores come from the attention map, not from the CLS token: regeneration difficulty (diagonal of attention) times broadcasting ability (received attention), max over heads, so it works without a CLS token. The P lowest tokens per layer are removed and their features are propagated (added with a weight alpha) to kept neighbours on a graph built once after embedding from spatial adjacency and cosine similarity (operation 'other' = graph propagation of pruned features into several kept tokens). Proportional attention and attention-map sparsification are added. Costs are GMACs. Throughput on an A6000 with batch 128. Main results are training-free; a 30-epoch finetuned variant is also reported (79.7 at 3.5 GMACs).
evidence: "GTP meticulously propagates less significant tokens' information to spatially and semantically connected tokens that are of greater importance" (Abstract); "we keep N - P tokens with the largest Gamma x Psi values and propagate the rest P tokens" (3.2.1); "GTP decreases the computational complexity of both DeiT-S and DeiT-B by up to 26% with only a minimal 0.3% accuracy drop on ImageNet-1K without finetuning" (Abstract); "we utilize the same data augmentation and training recipe as implemented in DeiT [38] and finetune for only 30 epochs" (4.1)

name: Zero-TPrune
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; LV-ViT-S; LV-ViT-M; AugReg ViT; MAE ViT; SWAG ViT
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.4 at 2.97 GFLOPs (no fine-tuning; baseline 79.8 at 4.55)
notes: I-stage: the attention matrix is treated as a directed graph and a Weighted Page Rank (30/5/1 iterations by depth) gives importance scores; heads are combined by root-mean-square (EIR) and filtered by variance (VHF); the CLS token gets a larger initial score. S-stage: tokens are split by importance rank and one token of each of the top-r most similar pairs (cosine of keys) is pruned. Order I'-S-I. Retention rates per pruning layer are fixed hyperparameters (optionally searched by Monte Carlo). Throughput on one A100 with batch 512. Main results are training-free; a fine-tuned variant is shown in Fig. 6 and Supp. C. The code cell is the project page given in the paper. Code: the project page jha-lab.github.io/zerotprune gives no code.
evidence: "the first zero-shot method that considers both the importance and similarity of tokens in performing token pruning. It leverages the attention graph of pre-trained Transformer models to produce an importance distribution for tokens via our proposed Weighted Page Rank (WPR) algorithm" (Abstract); "We retain the top-k important tokens (k is determined by the retention rates and the total number of tokens)" (3.2); "We prune one token in each selected pair instead of merging them" (3.3); "Without any fine-tuning, Zero-TPrune reduces the FLOPs cost of DeiT-S by 34.7% and improves its throughput by 45.3% with only 0.4% accuracy loss" (Abstract)

name: PaPr
backbones: ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; ViT-H/16 (AugReg, MAE); ViT-Medium-GAP; DeiT-S; ConvNeXt-B; ConvNeXt-L; Swin-B; Swin-L; ViT-B/L MAE (video)
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.2 at 2.7 GFLOPs (z=0.55, trained; baseline 79.8 at 4.6); training-free ViT-B/16 AugReg: 82.11 at 8.98 GFLOPs (baseline 84.59 at 17.59)
notes: A pre-trained lightweight ConvNet (MobileOne-S0) with its FC weights set uniform gives a patch significance map (channel mean of the last conv features, upsampled); the top-z% patches are kept in one step right after patch embedding (criterion 'other' = external ConvNet saliency, no training of the selector). Also applied to ConvNeXt and Swin (pixel operators run only on kept patches, rest zero-padded) and to video (Kinetics-400, ViT-MAE). The DeiT-S row comes from the training comparison (Table 4: PaPr trained, 1.6x training speed); all other rows are training-free. Throughput on one RTX A5000, batch size not stated.
evidence: "we introduce PaPr, a method for substantially pruning redundant patches with minimal accuracy loss using lightweight ConvNets across a variety of deep learning architectures, including ViTs, ConvNets, and hybrid transformers, without any re-training" (Abstract); "we identify the indices corresponding to the top-z% patches as per M, facilitating the retention of only the most salient patches in F" (3.2); "our approach seeks to eliminate redundant tokens early in the processing pipeline, immediately following initial patch extraction" (3.3); "We report training-free results of PaPr, unless otherwise specified" (4.1)

name: Cropr
main_result: ViT-L (MAE): top-1 85.3 at 1480 img/s (1.7x; baseline 85.8 at 860 img/s, A100); EVA-02-L 448px: top-1 89.7 at 0.18 TFLOPs (2.1x; baseline 89.9 at 0.31)
notes: A Cropr module after every block scores tokens with a single-head cross-attention scorer with learnable queries and keeps the Top-K (R tokens pruned per block, constant per image); an aggregator plus auxiliary task head train the scorer end-to-end (stop-gradient to the backbone) and are removed at inference, where the router reduces to a vector-matrix product. Last Layer Fusion reinserts all pruned tokens before the final block for dense tasks (ADE20k Segmenter, COCO Cascade Mask R-CNN). The backbone is fine-tuned together with the modules. Throughput on an A100 with AMP, best over batch sizes. No DeiT-S.
evidence: "we present a token pruner that uses auxiliary prediction heads that learn to select tokens end-to-end based on task relevance. These auxiliary heads can be removed after training" (Abstract); "The scorer itself is modeled after a cross-attention module with learnable queries" (3.1); "we use a throughput-optimized static approach that prunes a constant number of tokens to enable batching across inputs" (2); "pruned tokens from all Cropr modules are inserted alongside retained tokens output by the penultimate ViT block" (3.3); "We fine-tune ViT-L on ImageNet-1k using a pretrained masked autoencoder (MAE)" (4.1)

main_result: DINOv2-G (AGX Orin, batch 2): top-1 -2.04 points at 104.1 ms (-33.1% latency; baseline 155.5 ms)
notes: Offline, for a model-device pair, latency L(n) is measured for every token count n and accuracy A(n) is estimated by random pruning after the first layer; the number of tokens R to prune maximises 0.5*U_A + 0.5*U_L, exploiting non-linear latency-workload steps (GPU tail effect). All R tokens are pruned once after the first 25% of layers. Tokens are ranked by received attention (max over heads) plus a V-matrix magnitude term; pruned tokens are averaged into one inattentive token as in EViT. DeiT-S results are given only as accuracy drop and latency (TX2 batch 2: -1.24 points at 49.44 ms; batch 1: -0.99 points at 32.12 ms), no absolute accuracy or FLOPs. The paper says the code is open source but gives no URL.
evidence: "we determine token pruning schedule by leveraging non-linear latency-workload relationships. Third, we demonstrate a training-free, token pruning method utilizing this schedule" (Abstract); "Our schedule prunes all R tokens at one layer, early in the model" (3.2); "we rank token importance by measuring the attention each token receives from all others, utilizing the softmax attention matrix. We also incorporate an importance term derived from the V matrix" (3.3); "instead of discarding pruned tokens, we create a new "inattentive" token based on the features of all pruned tokens" (3.3)

name: Static Routing
backbones: ViT-T; ViT-S; ViT-B; ViT-L; DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; AugReg ViT-B; DINOv3 ViT-B; SigLIP ViT-B
main_result: DeiT-B: top-1 80.0 at 10.0 GFLOPs, 2705 img/s (baseline 81.7 at 17.6, 2044 img/s), RTX 5090, without retraining
notes: Read from the published article (CC BY 4.0) supplied by the authors. Each block prunes a fixed ratio of patch tokens and uses either the CLS-to-patch attention or a non-attention score (default: kNN cosine uniqueness, Eq. 6), chosen per layer by a static routing map built offline on a calibration subset (attention-selectivity rule, restricted search, or two-stage search). No retraining, no per-image control. Data available on request, no code link. Throughput batch size not stated.
evidence: "lightweight static routing configurations are investigated without retraining or dynamic inference control" (Abstract); "pi_l in {attn, alt} specifies whether attention-based or non-attention pruning is used at layer l. All routing decisions are made offline and remain fixed during inference" (Sec. 5.1); "A fixed pruning ratio is applied at each transformer layer" (Sec. 3); Table 4: DeiT-S Static Routing 78.0 / 2.6 G / 6696 img/s, DeiT-B 80.0 / 10.0 G / 2705; "the static routing results reported here employ the kNN-based importance criterion" (Sec. 5.5); "Data will be made available on request" (Data availability)

backbones: ViT-S; Hybrid ViT-S (ResNet26 stem); ViT-L; Hybrid ViT-L (ResNet50 stem)
main_result: ViT-L: top-1 80.62 at -50.44% FLOPs and -46.8% latency (Top-K+VPA, pruning rate 6%, ImageNet-1k, GPU)
notes: Read from the published article (Applied Intelligence 55, 342) in the authors' copy. Gradient-Aware Scaling (GAS) adjusts the per-layer pruning rate during fine-tuning so that the training loss converges (rate learned, not per image), applied to Top-K, EViT, eTPS, and ToMe on six small datasets. Variable Proportional Attention (VPA) for Top-K keeps the selection of Top-K by the attention to [CLS] and folds the removed tokens into the size vector of proportional attention by their cosine similarity to the kept tokens, with a variable temperature. Top-K+VPA is also applied without training to an off-the-shelf ViT-L on ImageNet-1k. No DeiT-S results; no code link in the article; latency is the time of one query divided by the batch size, and the batch size of the timing is not stated.
evidence: "The proposed pruning rate adjustment adjusts the pruning rate so that the training loss is converged by Gradient-Aware Scaling (GAS)" (Abstract); "Top-K policy keeps the top k tokens with the highest contribution to the [CLS] in each layer" (Sec. 3); "this paper modifies row vector s to preserve the information of the tokens to be removed by aggregating their similarity to the tokens to be kept. VPA has a variable temperature" (Sec. 3); "pruning rate adjustments are made for Top-K, EViT, eTPS, and ToMe" (Sec. 4.1.4); "ImageNet-1k is used to evaluate the performance of pruning methods in the off-the-shell ViT model without training" (Sec. 4.1.2); Table 3: ViT-L Top-K+VPA 80.62 at r=6%, GPU latency 4.54 ms (-46.8%); "Latency measures the time to process one image by dividing the time to process one query by the batch size" (Sec. 4.1.5)

notes: Analysis paper (ICCVW 2023), not a method. Ten token reduction methods (Top-K, EViT, DynamicViT, ATS, ToMe, K-Medoids, DPC-KNN, SiT, PatchMerger, Sinkhorn) plus three fixed radial baselines are inserted at blocks 4/7/10 of DeiT-T/S/B, fine-tuned (30 epochs on ImageNet) and compared on ImageNet, NABirds, COCO and NUS-WIDE at keep rates 25-90%. Findings: Top-K and EViT are the strongest; pruning patterns are consistent across keep rates but not across backbone capacity; learned patterns differ from fixed centre-biased patterns; averaged patterns correlate across datasets; pattern similarity is a moderate-to-strong proxy for accuracy. Efficiency is not measured. DeiT-S ImageNet at r=70%: baseline 79.85, Top-K 79.22, EViT 79.30, ToMe 79.63 (Table 1). The code cell is the project page.
evidence: "we set out to understand the reduction patterns of 10 different token reduction methods using four image classification datasets. By systematically comparing these methods on the different classification tasks, we find that the Top-K pruning method is a surprisingly strong baseline" (Abstract); "the reduction patterns are generally not consistent when varying the capacity of the backbone model, the reduction patterns of pruning-based methods significantly differ from fixed radial patterns, and the reduction patterns of pruning-based methods are correlated across classification datasets" (Abstract); "this work does not evaluate the efficiency of the tested methods" (6)

name: ATC
backbones: DeiT-T; DeiT-S; DeiT-B; ViT-B; ViT-L; ViT-H (MAE); Stable Diffusion v1.5; ViT-Adapter-T; ViT-Adapter-S
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.82 at keep rate 70% (ATC-average, fine-tuned; baseline 79.85; FLOPs not reported); ViT-L MAE off-the-shelf: top-1 84.8 (constant t=8; ToMe 84.2; baseline 85.9)
notes: ToMe with the bipartite matching replaced by agglomerative (bottom-up hierarchical) clustering on the cosine distance of keys, with single, average or complete linkage; cluster members are averaged with size weighting and proportional attention; parameter-free. Reported off-the-shelf and after 30-epoch fine-tuning on DeiT (blocks 4/7/10, keep rates 25-90%), MAE ViT-B/L/H (per-block constant or linear schedule), Stable Diffusion (FID) and COCO ViT-Adapter. Largest gains at keep rates 25-50%; off-the-shelf DeiT-S collapses at r=25% (24.27). FLOPs are not reported. Throughput is only plotted (Fig. 11, A40 GPU, batch sizes 1 to 1024) and is below ToMe at large batch because the clustering runs on the CPU (scikit-learn). The code cell is the project page.
evidence: "ATC merges clusters through bottom-up hierarchical clustering, without the introduction of extra learnable parameters" (Abstract); "we use the cosine distance as our distance metric D(.) and the keys from the self-attention module as token features" (3.2); "In this paper we consider the static reduction scenario" (3.2); "we report both off-the-shelf results, where ATC is inserted into the pre-trained model and evaluated without any fine-tuning, and results after fine-tuning" (4)

backbones: DeiT-III ViT-B; OpenCLIP ViT-B/16; DINOv2 ViT-L/14; DINOv2 ViT-g/14
notes: Analysis paper (ICLR 2024), not a token reduction method. Supervised (DeiT-III), text-supervised (OpenCLIP) and self-supervised (DINOv2) ViTs produce a few (about 2%) high-norm outlier tokens (about 10x norm) from the middle layers of large, long-trained models; they sit on patches redundant with their neighbours (background), carry little local information but strong global information, i.e. the model reuses them as scratch space. Adding learnable register tokens removes the artifacts, keeps linear-probe accuracy, and improves dense tasks (ADE20k, NYUd) and object discovery (LOST). Relevant to token reduction because token norm and attention maps are used as importance scores. No code URL of its own in the paper (official DeiT, OpenCLIP and DINOv2 repositories are cited for training).
evidence: "The artifacts correspond to high-norm tokens appearing during inference primarily in low-informative background areas of images, that are repurposed for internal computations" (Abstract); "We observe that they are tokens with roughly 10x higher norm at the output and correspond to a small fraction of the total sequence (around 2%)" (1); "the model learns to recognize patches containing little useful information, and recycle the corresponding tokens to aggregate global image information while discarding spatial information" (1); "we observe that the outlier tokens disappear from the sequence entirely. As a result, the performance of the models increases in dense prediction tasks" (1)
